papers.title: Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Emerging Frontiers
papers.summary: Survey that formalizes agent memory as a write-manage-read loop coupled with perception and action, with a three-dimensional taxonomy (temporal scope, representational substrate, control mechanism). Covers five mechanism families, from context compression and retrieval stores to reflective self-improvement and policy-learned management, and argues evaluation should move to multi-session, decision-grounded tests.

papers.title: A Survey of Context Engineering for Large Language Models
papers.summary: Systematic survey of over 1,400 papers that treats context engineering as a discipline, splitting it into context retrieval and generation, processing, and management. It then shows how these components combine into RAG, memory systems, tool-integrated reasoning, and multi-agent systems, and highlights a gap between models' ability to understand complex contexts and to generate equally sophisticated long outputs.
